slides.title: Build it, or depend
body: Germany and Europe must move faster to build their own AI or risk becoming **dependent on outside providers**, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Monday at an AI conference in Berlin, according to Reuters.

slides.quote: **a truly existential question** … at all costs, avoid becoming entirely dependent on third parties
slides.who: Friedrich Merz, Germany's chancellor, on digital sovereignty

slides.title: Own the whole chain
body: Merz said Germany's ambition should be to develop and operate its own technology **from hardware to software**. He acknowledged that would take "an enormous technological and organisational effort."

slides.title: €225bn in pledges
body: At a summit last month, companies including Amazon and Nvidia joined pledges worth **more than €225bn**, according to Germany's economy ministry. Germany also aims to **quadruple its AI computing power by 2030**.

slides.title: Not ready yet
body: Germany's Ifo institute, an economics research body, found the country is **still not ready** to benefit fully from the AI boom, Reuters reported. It pointed to a small high-tech sector, weak digital public services and **skills shortages**.

facts.text: "Germany and Europe must move faster to build their own AI technology or risk becoming dependent on outside providers, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Monday, according to Reuters." Published 2026-11-02; "Speaking at an AI conference in Berlin".

Merz "called digital sovereignty 'a truly existential question' and said Germany must 'at all costs, avoid becoming entirely dependent on third parties.'" The quote slide shows only these two verbatim fragments, separated by an ellipsis; digital sovereignty is named in the attribution line.

"Germany's ambition, he said, should be to develop and operate its own technology across the entire supply chain, from hardware to software." Merz "acknowledged that reaching that point would require 'an enormous technological and organisational effort.'"

"At a summit last month, companies including Amazon and Nvidia joined pledges worth more than €225bn, according to the economy ministry. Germany also aims to quadruple its AI computing power by 2030." The article gives no pledger breakdown, period or baseline, and no exchange rate, so the post gives euros only.

"The Ifo economics institute found that Germany is still not ready to benefit fully from the AI boom, Reuters reported. Its assessment pointed to a relatively small high-tech sector, weak digital public services, skills shortages, and the country's continued reliance on paper-based processes." The post describes Ifo as an economics research body, from "Ifo economics institute".

caption:
Germany's chancellor Friedrich Merz just called digital sovereignty "a truly existential question."

Speaking at an AI conference in Berlin on Monday, Friedrich Merz said Germany and Europe must build their own AI faster or risk depending on outside providers, according to Reuters.

→ Merz: Germany must "at all costs, avoid becoming entirely dependent on third parties"
→ Companies including Amazon and Nvidia joined pledges worth more than €225bn at a summit last month, per the economy ministry; Germany aims to quadruple its AI computing power by 2030
→ Germany's Ifo institute found the country is still not ready to benefit fully from the AI boom, citing skills shortages and weak digital public services
